A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Learning normalized image densities via dual score matching. Their main text, equations, two tables, eight figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison; extraction difficulties were resolved through visual inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture experiments and ImageNet64 results, including denoising performance, likelihood estimates, generalization, and image-density analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports concrete training and probability-evaluation timings.

M1.justification: The space/time score-matching losses, weighting, normalization procedure, inner-product energy architecture, and UNet components remain unchanged. Appendix C.1 clarifies that the energy gradient must be computed directly; this documents the existing procedure rather than introducing a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture examples and color/grayscale ImageNet64 coverage. The added discussion of conditional models and out-of-distribution behavior does not report evaluations on new tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Glow, PixelCNN, I-DDPM, VDM, FM, NFDM, and TarFlow. Table 1 and Figure 1 retain their score-network and single-score-matching comparators. The timing comparison uses the existing score-network comparator; newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 2.4 adds a timing comparison for 50,000 images, specifying 100 integration steps and 10 noise samples for score-based energy computation, plus A100 training timings for one million steps. Existing accuracy-evaluation splits, preprocessing, metrics, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 1's single-versus-dual score-matching demonstration contains a very small vertical adjustment to the globally normalized single-score energy curve; its failure to recover the target energy remains unchanged. The other generalization, image-statistics, dimensionality, and example-image analyses are retained.

E5.justification: No independent-run counts, seed values, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests are added. Appendix C.3 retains the same maximum-likelihood Gumbel fitting and discussion of random-initialization dependence.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results, including the proposed model's 3.36 bits/dimension NLL. Beyond the tiny Figure 1 curve adjustment, v2 adds 12 seconds versus at least 3 hours 20 minutes for probability evaluation and 120 versus 32 hours for training. Appendix C.2 revises H100 training time from about four to five days. These are added or revised cost results, not an accuracy improvement.

T1.justification: The numbered mathematical definitions and equations, Appendix B derivations, and Appendix A.3 Poincaré conjecture are retained. Score-sign terminology and the connected-support explanation clarify the existing normalization argument without introducing a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain normalized energy learning through dual score matching, competitive NLL, strong generalization, broad energy variation, and image-dependent local dimensionality. The revised abstract explicitly describes the non-overlapping-subset test already reported in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds conditional-model applicability, links local dimensionality to comparable local probability masses, and connects Appendix A.4's volume argument to high densities for out-of-distribution samples. Section 2.4 explicitly interprets the losses as having coincident minima. The training-cost limitation changes from roughly doubled to quadrupled, with an added inference-efficiency tradeoff.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds explicit instructions to compute the energy gradient rather than substitute the underlying score-network output. Runtime and hardware disclosures are expanded, and the reported H100 training duration is revised. Hardware context remains ambiguous because Section 2.4 reports A100 timings while Appendix C.2 still says H100. Hyperparameters and code/model access information are retained.

R1.justification: The new Related approaches paragraph substantially clarifies the positioning of the central objective against Choi et al., Kobler and Pock, Yu et al., and Yadin et al. v2 identifies its time-score objective as a special case of concurrent Yu et al. work and acknowledges Thornton et al.'s concurrent inner-product parameterization. These qualifications concern both principal method components, beyond routine citation additions.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the abstract, motivation, normalization explanation, and results discussion, plus a Related approaches paragraph. The limitations paragraph is incorporated into Discussion, and the preprint footer becomes a NeurIPS 2025 notice. The overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The same two tables and eight figures are retained, with limited rendering and caption revisions. Table 1 and Figures 2 and 5 are relocated, and Appendix D's three image grids are consolidated onto one page. Figure 8's caption now specifies ordering from low to high probability.

improvement.justification: v2 improves attribution of the objective and architecture, supplies concrete computational-cost evidence, and clarifies an implementation detail important for reproduction. These are useful gains while the main validation and proofs remain stable. The timing hardware context is ambiguous, and the approximate-normalization warning is less prominent in the main text, although retained in Appendix A.3. Overall, the improvement is supported but limited.
